issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of this page covers only metrics, meters and tracing. The rendering guidance has moved to the performance/rendering subpage, which the rendering page excerpt itself references as "ASP.NET Core Blazor rendering performance best practices".

Update linkTitles to "Рекомендации по производительности отрисовки ASP.NET Core Blazor" (ru) and "ASP.NET Core Blazor rendering performance best practices" (en). Confirm that page covers ShouldRender and parameter change detection.

issues.claim: The behaviour is described for .NET 10 and has not changed since early Blazor versions.
issues.problem: The rendering docs excerpt says the rules and the known-type list "are subject to change at any time". The list has been extended over the years. Option d's explanation also says "fixed list". Both overstate stability.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with: "The behaviour is described for .NET 10; the set of known types is an implementation detail of the framework and may change." Reword "fixed list" in option d to "built-in list". Make the same change in ru.

issues.claim: Option a is much longer than b, c and d.
issues.problem: Option a is far longer than the others, so a candidate can pick it by length alone.
issues.suggestedFix: Shorten option a to a single sentence: "Фреймворк пропускает перерисовку только если все параметры известных неизменяемых типов и не изменились; параметр типа `Product` считается возможно изменившимся." Do the same in en.

issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/security/anti-request-forgery, cited for "Razor component endpoints require token validation by default. If UseAntiforgery is missing ... fails with an exception"
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt is the newer version of the page. It says apps that do not call app.UseAntiforgery() are protected by an automatic CSRF middleware, and the Razor Components endpoint no longer validates tokens itself. So the link as fetched does not support the .NET 10 claim that UseAntiforgery is mandatory. A reader following it on .NET 11 would be confused. The excerpt shows nothing of the "Endpoint ... contains anti-forgery metadata" exception or of placement after UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization.
issues.suggestedFix: Pin the link to the .NET 10 version (add ?view=aspnetcore-10.0) or cite the antiforgery section of the Blazor forms docs for .NET 10. Verify the exception text and the middleware placement there. Add one sentence to the explanation in both locales: this is the .NET 8-10 behaviour; .NET 11 changes it.

issues.claim: `EditForm` adds the hidden antiforgery token field to the form by itself. ... `Enhance` only replaces the full page reload with a `fetch` request
issues.problem: The forms page excerpt stops before the antiforgery section and before any mention of the `Enhance` parameter. It shows only a plain <form> with a manual <AntiforgeryToken />. These two claims (the automatic token in EditForm, and the existence and role of EditForm.Enhance) cannot be confirmed from the excerpt, although they match my recollection of the .NET 8-10 docs.
issues.suggestedFix: Check these claims against the .NET 10 forms page (the "Antiforgery support" and enhanced form handling sections). If confirmed, no text change is needed. Otherwise add a link to the page that states them.

issues.claim: "`middleware` защиты от подделки запросов в конвейере"
issues.problem: The English word is put in code format in the middle of a Russian sentence, which reads unnaturally.
issues.suggestedFix: "Промежуточное ПО защиты от подделки запросов в конвейере: `app.UseAntiforgery()`." Use the same wording in the explanation, in place of "не найден `middleware`".
